question.prompt:
In triangles \(ABC\) and \(DEF,\) lengths \(AC,\) \(BC,\) \(DF\) and \(EF\) are all equal. Length \(AB\) is twice the length of the altitude of \(\triangle DEF\) from \(F\) to \(DE.\) Which of the following statements is (are) true?

\(\mathrm{I}.\) \(\angle ACB\) and \(\angle DFE\) must be complementary.

\(\mathrm{II}.\) \(\angle ACB\) and \(\angle DFE\) must be supplementary.

\(\mathrm{III}.\) The area of \(\triangle ABC\) must equal the area of \(\triangle DEF.\)

\(\mathrm{IV}.\) The area of \(\triangle ABC\) must equal twice the area of \(\triangle DEF.\)

solutions.explanation:
Both triangles are isosceles. Their altitudes to their bases therefore bisect both the bases and the apex angles. This lets us use the given relation between a base and an altitude to compare right triangles.

Let \(M\) be the foot of the altitude from \(C\) to \(AB\), and let \(N\) be the foot of the altitude from \(F\) to \(DE\). Write \(FN=h>0\) and \(DN=d>0\). Then \(DE=2d\), while the given condition says \(AB=2h\), so \(AM=h=FN\).

The right triangles \(AMC\) and \(FND\) have equal hypotenuses \(AC=FD\) and equal legs \(AM=FN\). They are congruent by the hypotenuse-leg criterion. Consequently,
\[
CM=ND=d,\qquad \angle ACM=\angle FDN.
\]
Since the altitudes bisect the apex angles, the two acute angles in right triangle \(FND\) give
\[
\frac{\angle ACB}{2}+\frac{\angle DFE}{2}
=\angle FDN+\angle DFN=90^\circ.
\]
Thus \(\angle ACB+\angle DFE=180^\circ\). Statement II is true and statement I is false.

The areas are
\[
[ABC]=\frac12(2h)d=hd,
\qquad
[DEF]=\frac12(2d)h=hd.
\]
Here brackets denote area. These areas are equal and positive, so statement III is true and statement IV is false. Therefore II and III only are true, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Compare the right-triangle halves
